messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — CI canary shows a perf regression after the prefix-cache change we merged yesterday. p99 latency up ~9% on nv4s.

maria: ugh, really? which stage — batching or kernel hotpath?

alex: looks like kernel selection; profiler shows more switches to the fallback long-seq kernel when cache hit rate is high.

jin: that sounds plausible. cache hits shrink the user-visible sequence length, but our kernel chooser still sees the original max_len and picks kernels based on allocated tensor size.

sam: do we have a short repro? I can run an A/B with and without the cache for the same prompt mix.

alex: yes. repro script:
```
# generate 1k requests with 60% prefix hits
python tools/stress_clients.py --scenario prefix_cache --ratio 0.6 --seq 512 --batch-size 64
```
profile output snippet:
```
kernel_choice: aten_conv_long (fallback)  ->  42%  (expected aten_fast 78%)
avg_effective_len: 64  avg_alloc_len: 512
p99: baseline 210ms -> canary 228ms
```

maria: so effective runtime length (post-cache) is small but admission/packer uses allocated length -> packing creates fewer tokens per batch => different kernel, worse throughput.

jin: I think two things: batching heuristic should use 'effective_length' (user_len - cached_prefix) for token_budget accounting; and kernel selector should prefer kernels based on runtime sequence distribution, not allocation size.

sam: agree. small experiment idea: add a per-request field effective_len and have packer compute token_budget using that. cheap to try.

perf-bot: benchmark queued: run/2024-07/cache-hit-effective-test started by sam

alex: also noticed stalling when a few large allocated requests join a batch of many cached-short ones — kernel swap causes SLOB on SMs. Can we add a soft cap: if >80% of batch have eff_len < X, force small-sequence kernel?

jin: yep. proposal: packer -> compute median_eff_len per batch; if median_eff_len < threshold, mark batch as 'short' and tag kernel_hint=fast_short.

maria: sounds good. add telemetry: record median_eff_len and kernel_hint mismatch count so we can verify.

sam: I'll prototype patch tonight, run canary against prod traffic sample.

alex: thanks. leave the canary running; if sam's patch looks good we'll revert the prefix-cache change until we have packer/kernel fixes in place. :thumbsup:
